alt: Top: bars of bits per number for the starter code on the docids dataset. The checker's stored reference is 5.13, left of a dashed line at the 8-bit minimum for any whole-byte format; the starter actually measures 38.98. Bottom left: the unchanged starter's raw result is 0.23 on the original checker and 0.98 on the fixed checker, against a dashed line at the documented 1.0. Bottom right: the best submission of a real agent run scores 75.72 out of 100 as recorded by the run and 53.95 out of 100 when regraded with the fixed checker.
caption: The checker compares every submission with a stored reference for the starter code that the starter cannot reach, so every score is off. The task is to improve an integer compressor; on the docids dataset the stored reference is 5.13 bits per number, below the 8 bits any whole-byte format needs, while the starter actually uses 38.98 (5 of the 8 datasets have stored values below 8). As a result the unchanged starter scores 0.23 raw instead of the documented 1.0, and every raw result is too low by a factor that differs per dataset. The fixed checker measures the starter in the same run (0.98 raw for the starter) and puts the starter at 0 and the formula's maximum of 320 at 100 on its 0 to 100 scale, so the best submission of a real Claude Opus 5.5 run, recorded at 75.72 out of 100, regrades to 53.95 out of 100.
